findings.title: Denial cache conflates anonymous and renderer identities
findings.body: The denial key contains only `UserUID`, not `IdentityType`. Both `anonymous:0` and `render:0` therefore use the same key for a namespace/action/resource/folder. If an anonymous request is denied for a private dashboard, line 154 stores that denial; a subsequent renderer check for the same dashboard exits at line 117 as denied even though `getRendererPermissions` would grant dashboard reads. This permits cross-identity cache poisoning and can be used to keep renderer access denied by repeatedly causing anonymous checks. Include the identity type (or the full subject) in the denial-cache key.

findings.title: Denial cache key encoding is ambiguous for valid resource UIDs
findings.body: `name` and `parent` are concatenated with `_` without escaping or length-prefixing. For example, a denial for name `a_b` with parent `c` produces the same key as a check for name `a` with parent `b_c`. Dashboard and folder UIDs can contain underscores, so a denial for one resource can incorrectly short-circuit an allowed check for another resource for 30 seconds. Use an unambiguous structured encoding or a hash of separately serialized fields.

findings.title: Per-resource denial entries allow unbounded cache cardinality
findings.body: Every denied check writes a distinct cache entry derived from the caller-supplied resource name and folder. A caller can issue checks for continuously changing nonexistent resource IDs, causing both the database fallback and one new denial-cache entry per request. The in-process service uses a local cache without a capacity limit at construction, and expired entries may remain until its cleanup interval, so this turns arbitrary request cardinality into cache memory growth. Use a size-bounded/admission-controlled cache or avoid caching arbitrary negative resource lookups.

findings.title: Explicit-denial-cache test does not prove the denial cache is consulted
findings.body: The test comment says the normal permission cache should allow access if checked, but it stores `"dashboards:uid:dash1": false`. Without the new denial-cache lookup, `Check` would still return denied from that false value (and then from the empty fake store), so the test passes even if the denial cache is removed or bypassed. Store `true` for the dashboard scope and assert that no permission-store lookup occurs, so the test verifies denial-cache precedence.
